text:
anya: Heads up — Grafana shows a big spike in `heartbeat_missed` for ws sessions starting ~12:03 UTC but raw logs show pings arriving. Weird duplication in counts. :thinking:
kevin: Hmm. Which dashboard/query are you looking at? can you paste the panel query?
anya: panel is `Streaming -> Connections -> heartbeat_missed (per minute)` with `group by shard,env` and `sum(rate(telemetry.heartbeat_missed[1m]))` on the collector metric. I grabbed the raw logs for one session:```
2026-03-08T12:02:59Z ws:session=6f9a0 heartbeat=recv sampler=0.25 aggregator=collector-a shard=us-west-2
2026-03-08T12:03:00Z ws:session=6f9a0 heartbeat=missed sampler=0.25 aggregator=collector-b shard=us-west-2
```
kevin: oof aggregator changed mid-session — that smells like duplicate counting in the metrics path. metrics-bot: alert fired: `heartbeat_missed > 1000` (1m) at 2026-03-08T12:04:00Z :rotating_light:
sre-oncall: Did we roll the telemetry-proxy yesterday? there was a sampling change to route low-sample sessions to second-tier collectors.
david: yeah we rolled a sampling change at 02:00 PT — it introduced a new `sampler_id` header that both collectors are using to emit metrics. If a request/stream gets proxied between collectors during a stickiness window, we might record both recv and missed across different aggregator tags.
anya: That would explain why the dashboard shows a spike while the session logs look fine. the dashboard groups by `shard,env` but not by `sampler_id` or `aggregator`, so counts from both collectors collapse into one time series and inflate the rate.
ui-ops: Quick repro idea: tail the collector metrics and log the `aggregator` tag per metric for a single session while inducing a proxy handoff. If we see `heartbeat_missed` emitted by two different aggregator tags for same session-ts, it's the duplication.
kevin: I ran a local repro: handoff triggers two emit paths because the collector flush path retries on connection break and doesn't mark idempotency. snippet from the metrics emitter:```
// pseudo
emitMetric(name, tags) {
  if (!retryInProgress) {
    transport.send({name,tags})
  } else {
    // retry path also sends without the idempotency key
    transport.send({name,tags})
  }
}
```
david: so two sends, same metric name, different aggregator tag. aggregator tag is added in the proxy layer, not the emitter, so the idempotency key is lost on retry. Not great.
anya: Can we fix by adding an `idempotency_key` tag in the emitter and preserving it across retries so the TSDB dedupes? or change dashboard to group by aggregator too as short-term mitigation.
sre-oncall: Short-term: update Grafana panels to include `aggregator` in grouping and add a note on the dashboard doc. Long-term: prefer emitter-level dedupe or include `sampler_id`/`idempotency_key` in the metric tags upstream.
kevin: I'll open a small PR to add the idempotency tag on the emitter and also change the retry path to reuse it. low-risk.
david: Also need a fix in telemetry-proxy to preserve the header on reconnects (it's being dropped on new TCP connection). I'll file a follow-up.
ui-ops: For now I patched the panel query to `group by shard,env,aggregator` and tweaked alert thresholds to avoid noisy pages. will roll that in the next dashboard deploy. :thumbsup:
metrics-bot: note: alert suppression set for `heartbeat_missed` for 30m after dashboard change by ui-ops.
anya: Thanks folks. Can we add a short postmortem blurb in the dashboard README explaining the sampler/aggregator caveat so SRE/SEs don't chase logs when it's a metric tagging mismatch?
sre-oncall: yes, add it to /docs/streaming-metrics/README.md and link from the panel. assigning to kevin for PR and david for proxy fix.
kevin: taking the PR for emitter idempotency tag. will have a patch by EOD and a canary tomorrow.
david: created issue #4122 for proxy header preservation and assigned to me.
anya: awesome. saved a bunch of time. :eyes:
